explanation: Find the lower bound: the first position whose value is at least k. It is the first occurrence if it equals k; otherwise the target is absent.
timeComplexity: O(log n). Each iteration halves the candidate interval, hence logarithmically many comparisons.
spaceComplexity: O(1). Only two endpoints, a midpoint and possibly one saved index are retained.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The half-open interval [left,right) retains the possible lower-bound position. Every discarded left value is less than k; every discarded right value is at least k. At convergence left is the first position with value at least k, so it is the first occurrence exactly when its value equals k.
walkthrough: For [-2,1,1,1,5] and k=1, lower-bound search keeps moving the right boundary left across equal 1 values. It converges at index 1, the first position containing 1, and returns 1.
edgeCases: Repeated targets return their first index.
A lower bound at array length means the target is absent.
Targets below the minimum still require an equality check.
